sketches.title: Till the Bitter End
sketches.premise: Two shoppers build the same high-street bill, one item at a time. On your turn, add an item whose price is exactly higher than the last item but still keeps the running total under the shop's limit; the first player who cannot add a legal item loses. The host treats every doomed purchase like a public financial execution.
sketches.criterion: The judge checks that the named item has a clear whole-pound price higher than the previous item and that the new total stays within the stated limit; rounding, secret discounts, repeats, and merely claiming affordability do not count.
sketches.move_shape: Name one ordinary shop item, give its whole-pound price, and state the new total: "I buy a toaster for £24; total £57."
sketches.first_card: Opening limit: £100. First card: "I buy a comic for £3; total £3."

sketches.title: Shop Window Shift
sketches.premise: Two rival window dressers take turns changing one feature of a high-street shop display: its colour, object, light, or position. Each change must make the display fit a new customer or occasion while keeping every earlier feature that still makes sense; the first contradiction collapses the window and loses. The host narrates the display as if it were a royal scandal in cheap glass.
sketches.criterion: The judge checks that one concrete display change serves a named customer or occasion and preserves the established scene; a random change, an impossible reversal, or a vague "make it better" fails.
sketches.move_shape: State the new display feature and why it suits the next customer: "For a rainy-day walker, I add a bright umbrella beside the blue coat."
sketches.first_card: "A bakery window shows three warm pies on a wooden shelf, lit by one yellow lamp."

sketches.title: Queue Jumpers
sketches.premise: Two people control a queue outside a high-street shop. Each turn, move one named person to a new position by giving a fair, plain reason tied to what is happening; the queue must remain a single order, and the first player who cannot justify a move loses. The host calls every flimsy excuse what it is: queue-jumping with a thesaurus.
sketches.criterion: The judge checks that exactly one person changes place for a specific public reason such as age, injury, appointment, or service need; convenience, bribery, and simply being impatient do not count.
sketches.move_shape: Name one person, their new place, and the reason: "The woman with the crutch moves ahead of the four tourists because she cannot stand long."
sketches.first_card: "Outside the cinema, the queue is: Maya, a courier, two tourists, an old man, and Sam."

sketches.title: Receipt Rumble
sketches.premise: Two cashiers compete to explain a strange high-street receipt. On each turn, add one purchase that makes the total, discount, or message on the receipt more revealing, while all earlier numbers must still work; the first impossible explanation loses. The host reads the losing theory like a detective novel written by a drunk till.
sketches.criterion: The judge checks that the new item or discount fits every stated receipt detail and advances one clear explanation; a contradiction, a made-up total, or a bigger version of an existing purchase fails.
sketches.move_shape: Add one item with a price and consequence: "The £2 umbrella explains the wet receipt, and its 20% discount makes the total £18."
sketches.first_card: "Receipt: 3 items, £20 total, one discount, and a large water stain."

sketches.title: Mall Map Mutiny
sketches.premise: Two explorers navigate a high-street map by naming the next shop or landmark and one reason it is reachable from the current place. Every move must shorten the journey to the target without inventing roads or teleporting; the first player who cannot make a legal step loses. The host gives directions with the confidence of a sat-nav that has personally ruined your afternoon.
sketches.criterion: The judge checks that the named place is adjacent by an ordinary street or visible route and brings the explorer closer to the target; wandering, backtracking, teleporting, and claiming a shortcut without a route do not count.
sketches.move_shape: Name the next location and route: "From the bookshop, I cross the road to the café, which is beside the station target."
sketches.first_card: "Map: library — café — shoe shop — bus stop; the target is the bus stop. Start at the library."

sketches.title: Brand-New Bargain
sketches.premise: Two shopkeepers invent a high-street product by combining one familiar item with one practical improvement. Each turn must make the product solve a different everyday problem without losing its original use; the first ridiculous or redundant upgrade loses. The host crowns the winner and bankrupts the loser with a flourish.
sketches.criterion: The judge checks that the move names one ordinary product, one distinct useful change, and a real problem it solves; mere decoration, a larger copy, or an improvement that destroys the original use does not count.
sketches.move_shape: Name the product, upgrade, and benefit: "I sell a lunchbox with a small clock in the lid, so children know when to eat."
sketches.first_card: "I sell a school backpack with a bright rain cover, so books stay dry."
